web_blocks.html: The tape on NBIL (NASDAQ: NBIL) is decisive. On November 13, 2026, NBIL closed at $4.95 in a severe Weinstein Stage 4 decline [1][38]. Its technical gate is CAP_REJECTED under the STAGE4_BELOW_STRUCTURAL_FLOOR setup [38]. NBIL has dropped -27.74% over 1 week, -71.71% over 1 month, -85.66% over 3 months, and -87.78% over 6 months [1][38]. It sits -92.77% below its $68.49 52-week high [1][38]. Every key moving average slopes down and caps rallies.

All three timeframes show pure Stage 4 distribution with no Stage 1 base [38]. On the Weekly (1W) chart, NBIL trades -81.76% below its 30-week SMA ($27.14) and -66.44% below its 10-week EMA ($14.75), with Weekly RSI(14) at 36.23 [38]. On the Daily (1D) chart, price ($4.95) sits -78.95% below the 200-day SMA ($23.52) and -72.94% below the 50-day SMA ($18.29) [38]. It also trails its 20-day SMA ($9.82) and 10-day SMA ($7.46) [38]. Daily RSI(14) is 34.00, ATR14 is $2.57 (51.9% of price), and Bollinger Band width is 221.82% [38].

The tactical 4-Hour (4H) chart shows no turn either [38]. NBIL stays pinned beneath its 20-EMA ($7.85) and 50-SMA ($11.21), with 4H RSI(14) at 34.52 and intraday_4h_turn: false [38]. Underlying NBIS confirms the breakdown. It closed at $115.88 (-9.92% on November 13) below its 50-day SMA ($194.60), 200-day SMA ($179.35), and 30-week SMA ($203.87), with RSI(14) at 35.79 [40]. Note that while facts_US_2026-11-13.json tags NBIS as Stage 1 (Basing) near its $109.00 swing low, snapshots_US_2026-11-13.json flags STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) below its $194.60 50-DMA and $179.35 200-DMA; both indicators confirm NBIS is not in a Stage 2 uptrend [40]. NBIL's next support is its 52-week low at $4.29, followed by Pivot S1 at $2.92 [38]. Resistance starts at $7.46–$9.82 and runs up to Pivot R1 at $23.86 and R2 at $37.61 [38].

web_blocks.title: Volume Distribution & Options Chain Audit (Zero New Capital Rule)

web_blocks.html: Volume on November 13 confirms heavy distribution. NBIL plunged -19.77% on 32.95 million shares, or 3.07x its 30-day average [1][38]. That selloff followed NBIS's November 12 Q3 release, where management hiked FY2026 CapEx to ~$27B and FY2027 CapEx to $40B–$45B [35][39]. High-volume drops near 52-week lows ($4.29) signal forced liquidation, not seller exhaustion [38].

Our audit of options_US_NBIL.json shows why options are also off-limits [38]. NBIL's 20-day realized volatility (303.1%) tops its ATM implied volatility (177.2%, tagged IV_CHEAP), yet chain liquidity is broken [38]. The snapshot prints a conditional February 19, 2027 (96 DTE) $15 / $25 Bull Call Debit Spread ($0.55 debit, $550 max loss on 10 contracts, $9,450 max profit, $15.55 breakeven or +214.14%) [38]. Look at the leg quotes: the $15 call has a $0.00 bid / $0.80 ask (OI 31), and the $25 call has a $0.00 bid / $0.60 ask (OI 370) [38]. Wide zero-bid spreads destroy execution edge on entry and exit. Because NBIL is graded FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL and REJECTED, deploy zero new equity or options capital into NBIL.

book_paragraphs: Price action is where fundamental flaws and mathematical drag become visible on the tape. As of November 13, 2026, NBIL closed at $4.95, down 19.77% in a single session on 32.95 million shares—more than triple its 30-day average volume. That single-day drop capped a brutal multi-month cascade: down 27.74% over one week, 71.71% over one month, 85.66% over three months, and 92.77% from its 52-week high of $68.49.

Under Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis framework, NBIL is locked in an unmistakable Stage 4 decline. On the weekly chart, the ETF sits nearly 82% below its falling 30-week simple moving average at $27.14 and more than 66% below its 10-week EMA at $14.75. On the daily chart, price is 78.95% below its 200-day SMA ($23.52) and 72.94% below its 50-day SMA ($18.29), while 14-day ATR has expanded to $2.57—meaning an average daily swing equals more than half of the entire share price.

Nor is there any sign of an early intraday turn on the 4-hour chart, where NBIL remains pinned beneath its $7.85 20-EMA and $11.21 50-SMA with RSI at 34.52. Meanwhile, underlying Nebius Group (NBIS) dropped 9.92% on November 13 to $115.88, breaking well below its own 50-day ($194.60), 200-day ($179.35), and 30-week ($203.87) averages. Until NBIS itself stops falling and builds a multi-month Stage 1 base, NBIL cannot stabilize.

book_subsections.title: Why the Options Chain Is a Liquidity Trap
paragraphs: When an ETF falls 92% and its 20-day realized volatility surges to 303.1%, options market makers widen their spreads defensively. Although ATM implied volatility at 177.2% screens statistically cheap relative to realized volatility, the February 19, 2027 $15/$25 call spread illustrates the trap: the $15 strike has a $0.00 bid against a $0.80 ask with only 31 contracts of open interest, and the $25 strike sits at $0.00 bid / $0.60 ask. Paying a $0.55 debit for a spread that requires NBIL to rally +214% to $15.55 just to break even is negative-expectancy speculation.

Volume distribution on November 13 confirms that institutional and retail sellers are still exiting rather than accumulating. The 32.95 million shares traded on that -19.77% decline represent more than three times the 30-day average volume, occurring directly after Nebius Group's November 12 earnings release. In Stage Analysis, high-volume breakdown days near 52-week lows ($4.29) signal forced liquidation and margin calls, not durable seller exhaustion. Nearest structural support below $4.29 sits at Pivot S1 ($2.92), while overhead supply begins immediately at the 10-day SMA ($7.46) and 20-day SMA ($9.82).
Because NBIL fails fundamental quality checks (FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL) and carries a REJECTED verdict, our capital-preservation discipline is absolute: deploy zero new equity or options capital into NBIL.

In practical terms, an investor who waits for a confirmed Stage 1 base and Stage 2 breakout above a rising 30-week moving average will sacrifice the first few points off a theoretical bottom, but they avoid the devastating drawdowns that destroy capital during Stage 4 waterfalls. Right now, with NBIL 78.95% below its 200-day moving average and 81.76% below its 30-week moving average, there is no technical edge in either the shares or the options chain.

In addition, the 4-hour chart confirms that short-term momentum traders are not stepping in to defend the $4.95 level: both the 20-period EMA at $7.85 and the 50-period SMA at $11.21 are sloping sharply lower, and 4-hour RSI sits at 34.52 with no bullish divergence. Until NBIS itself reclaims its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and NBIL forms a multi-week horizontal base above support, any rally should be treated as a dead-cat bounce rather than a trend reversal.

Walk through the three-timeframe tape like a disciplined portfolio manager before you ever touch an order ticket. Start on the Weekly chart, which sets the primary tide: NBIL sits at $4.95 against a 30-week simple moving average of $27.14 and a 10-week EMA of $14.75, with weekly RSI at 36.23. That is an 81.76% deficit below the long-term institutional trend line. Next, drop to the Daily chart to inspect intermediate momentum: NBIL is 78.95% below its 200-day SMA ($23.52) and 72.94% below its 50-day SMA ($18.29), while 14-day ATR has ballooned to $2.57—more than half the share price in a typical daily range—and Bollinger Band width sits at 221.82%. Finally, check the 4-Hour chart for early basing clues: price remains trapped under both the $7.85 20-EMA and $11.21 50-SMA with no intraday turn.

Look at underlying Nebius Group (NBIS) as well, because NBIL cannot heal until NBIS heals first. On November 13, NBIS fell 9.92% to $115.88, sitting well below its $194.60 50-day SMA, $179.35 200-day SMA, and $203.87 30-week SMA with RSI at 35.79. Even though our facts ledger tags NBIS as Stage 1 (Basing) near its $109.00 swing low, our Stage 2 evaluation snapshot flags NBIS as STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) beneath its 50-day and 200-day averages. Both lenses agree on the only rule that matters for your capital: NBIS is nowhere near a Stage 2 uptrend, and buying a 2x daily ETF on a Stage 4 underlying is compounding risk on top of a broken trend.

book_callouts.title: Zero-Bid Options & Stage 4 Rule
book_callouts.text: Never deploy options capital into a Stage 4 leveraged ETF with $0.00-bid option legs. With NBIL graded FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL and REJECTED, both new equity purchases and conditional call spreads are strictly off-limits.
